predecessors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
predecessors.text: Málaga, where Yahya I al-Mu'tali, the Hammudid caliph at Córdoba until 1026, returned and declared independence

successors.name: Emirate of Granada
successors.text: Málaga, conquered by Granada in 1239 (1238 in the page text)

ledger.x: 1026: Yahya I al-Mu'tali, the Hammudid claimant to the caliphate of Córdoba, returns to Málaga and declares it an independent taifa.
1035: Yahya I annexes Algeciras to Málaga.
1039: Algeciras is Muhammad ibn al-Qasim's again.
1073: Badis dies and Málaga 'went to Tamim ben Buluggin ben Badis', a separate Zirid taifa from Granada under Abd Allah (Tamim 1073-1090 in the succession table).
1153: the Almohads take Málaga; Abu'l-Hakam kills himself (Almohad rule 1153-1229 in the table).
1229: Málaga 'became shortly independent in 1229' under Ibn Zannun as Almohad rule collapsed.
1239: the Taifa of Málaga ends; the land passes to Granada, which Cliopatria's Emirate of Granada row (from 1241) continues.

wars.name: Battle of Écija (1039)
wars.outcome: A Malagan victory on the Málaga page, a Zirid victory over the Abbadids of Seville near Écija on the Granada page; neither page names ground that changed hands.

wars.name: Zirid annexation of Málaga
wars.outcome: Badis of Granada annexed Málaga after Hammudid rule collapsed; the Hammudids fell back on Ceuta.

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the taifas
wars.outcome: Granada fell in September 1090 (Taifa of Granada page) and Málaga to the Almoravids in the same year (Málaga page).

certainty.note: The pages name cities and no boundaries; every extent is a reading of the province or a radius around a town.
